name: New Orleans by Night: Locations of Note

text.content: The Guilbeau family's ancestral plantation, several miles west of New Orleans, where Marcel and his brother Jereaux grew up as mortals and where Marcel still retreats whenever a difficult decision, or a threat requiring Jereaux's discreet intervention, demands his absence from the city. It is Marcel's true haven and, unofficially, the seat from which the city's real power is exercised.

pages.name: Metairie Cemetery and the New Orleans Cemeteries

text.content: Once the racetrack of the Metairie Jockey Club, converted into a cemetery in 1873 out of spite after its founder was denied membership, Metairie is the largest and best-kept of New Orleans' many cemeteries, its oval shape and circular drive tracing the vanished track. The city's numerous cemeteries as a group serve Kindred society as recognized sanctuary for refugees, with some of the less-maintained grounds (Lafayette Cemeteries No. 1 and No. 2 in particular) especially favored for their neglected, decaying tombs. St. Louis Cemetery No. 1 holds the monolithic tomb of Voodoo Queen Marie Laveau, still marked with pilgrims' X's and pennies left for good luck.

The only bayou remaining within city limits, running the length of City Park's eastern side to Lake Pontchartrain. Vampires use it as a convenient dumping ground for Lupines slain within the city — without realizing that the Uktena tribe of Garou has always considered the bayou sacred burial ground, a standing and unrecognized insult that could ignite the treaty between the two groups if ever discovered.

A French Quarter club owned by the Toreador leader Morgaine, though she keeps her true home elsewhere in the Garden District. It serves as an informal gathering point for the city's numerous transient Toreador, many of whom pass through New Orleans only briefly to enjoy its jazz and nightlife.

pages.name: Cajun Country and the Northern Teche

text.content: The bayous and backcountry surrounding New Orleans, contested territory between the Uktena tribe of Garou and the corrupting influence of the Wyrm, with Black Spiral Dancers rumored to be active in the area alongside Doran's old nemesis, a creature named Cosa. The insane Gangrel outcast Uriah Travers maintains a cabin in the northern Teche and has become the region's foremost authority on its secrets, respected (if not entirely trusted) even by the Uktena themselves.

vtmlarp.source: New Orleans by Night, Chapter Three: Geography
